concerns.text: Task T013 mandates generating 48 unique variants (3×2×2×4 scenarios) but the spec (FR-001) and plan only define the factorial structure (3×2×2=12). The task assumes a specific number of base scenarios (4) not defined in the spec, making the deliverable ambiguous. The implementer cannot determine the base scenarios to generate without external context.

Task T027 requires generating a 'Length-Dominance' hypothesis with specific weights (0.1/0.2/0.7) and citing literature (Hancock & Dunham, Derks et al.) for it. However, FR-005 explicitly lists only three operationalizations (Equal, Emoji-Dominant, Punctuation-Dominant) with specific weights (0.33/0.33/0.33, 0.6/0.2/0.2, 0.2/0.6/0.2). The task introduces a fourth, unauthorized hypothesis and arbitrary weights, making the deliverable non-compliant with the spec and unverifiable against the requirement.

Task T037-Mock sets a warning threshold at 2,160 seconds (36 minutes) but the spec (SC-005) requires the pipeline to complete within 6 hours (21,600 seconds). The task's verification logic ('If total_duration_seconds > 21600... DO NOT FAIL') fails to enforce the 6-hour constraint defined in the spec, making the verification step insufficient to confirm the success criteria.

Task T015b-Code specifies parsing a Prolific export with columns 'Q1...Q40'. The spec (US-1) only mentions a 1-7 Likert scale for support, not 40 questions. The task assumes a specific survey structure (40 columns) not defined in the spec, risking implementation failure if the actual survey has a different number of questions. The task needs to define the exact column mapping or reference the survey design document.

Task T007 requires defining 'VARIANCE_PARAMS' as a dictionary with keys 'random_effect_variance' and 'residual_variance' but marks them as 'deprecated fallback defaults'. The task does not specify the default numeric values for these parameters, leaving the implementer to guess the fallback values. The task must provide the specific default values or reference a source for them.
